Bru

Privacy policy

Last updated 16 August 2026.

Bru links your phone to a client you control, over a direct, end-to-end-encrypted connection. There is no Bru account, no Bru server, and no analytics or tracking of any kind. Nothing you read or send through Bru is stored outside your phone and browser.

What the app accesses on your phone

  • SMS messages. Bru reads messages from your phone's own SMS store and sends messages on your behalf. Messages are relayed only to the client you paired with.
  • Contacts. Read only to show names in place of bare phone numbers. Contact data is never sent anywhere except to your own paired client, as part of showing you who a conversation is with.
  • Clipboard text. Text you explicitly choose to share, in either direction, when you use the clipboard feature. Bru does not read your clipboard in the background.
  • Camera. Used solely to scan the pairing QR code. No image is stored or transmitted. Pairing can be completed with a typed code instead.

Where that data goes

To the single client you paired with, and nowhere else. Pairing is a deliberate act: you scan a QR code or type a pairing code, which establishes a cryptographic identity for that one client. Bru will not talk to any other peer.

The connection is end-to-end encrypted between your phone and your client. No one except you can read it.

Third parties in the connection path

Bru uses iroh to connect the two devices, which relies on public discovery and relay infrastructure operated by number 0. In practice this means:

  • Your device's public key and current network addresses are published to that discovery service, so your two devices can find each other.
  • When a direct connection between your phone and your client cannot be established, traffic is forwarded through a relay server. Relayed traffic stays end-to-end encrypted; the relay forwards bytes it cannot read.
  • That infrastructure can therefore observe that two devices are connected, and their IP addresses, but not the content of anything you send.

What is stored, and where

  • On your phone. A local database of the messages Bru has seen, your device's private key, and the identity of the client you paired with. Clearing the app's data or uninstalling it removes all of this.
  • In your client. Each client keeps its own private key, its record of the paired phone, and the message history it has received in local storage on that device. Unpairing clears all of it.

Children

Bru is not directed at children and collects nothing from anyone, of any age.

Your data is yours

Because we hold no data about you, there is nothing for us to hand over, correct, or delete on request. You can remove everything Bru holds by clearing the app's data or uninstalling it, and by unpairing in your client.

Changes

If this policy changes, the updated version appears on this page with a new date above.
